evidence.assay_type: clinical trial adverse event reporting (skin rash)
evidence.experimental_conditions: SPARTAN trial (NCT01946204) in nmCRPC patients; placebo-controlled
evidence.support_text: Apalutamide showed a higher rate of reported skin rash (all grades) compared with placebo in the SPARTAN trial (23.8% versus 5.5%). The delayed onset, response to immunosuppressive treatment, and recurrence following re-challenge suggests the rash may be mediated via an immune mechanism.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Combined phase 3 trials in CRPC patients
evidence.support_text: When safety data from all phase 3 trials involving patients with CRPC who were treated with enzalutamide were combined (n = 2799), the reported incidence of all grade skin rash (all preferred terms of rash) was 4.4% in the groups treated with enzalutamide and 2.8% in the placebo group (n = 1898); the incidence of grade ≥3 rash was 0.1% and 0.2%, respectively.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patients with mCSPC; apalutamide dose not specified
evidence.support_text: In the TITAN trial of patients with mCSPC, all-grade rash was increased with apalutamide (n = 524) compared with placebo (n = 527) (27.1% versus 6.3%); grade ≥3 rash was also elevated in apalutamide-treated patients versus placebo (6.3% versus 0.6%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: skin biopsies from patch test area and normal skin of epoxy resin-allergic patients; diene conjugates measured by UV absorbance at 234 nm
evidence.support_text: In the table, for epoxy resin-allergic patients, diene conjugates in normal skin: 234.4±117.0, in patch test area: 265.0±91.5. No significant increase was reported.

evidence.assay_type: human clinical case (contact sensitivity with histological examination)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Patient exposed to 9-bromofluorene during chemical synthesis; exposure via splashing, dust, or vapour. Histology of flare-up reaction showed epidermal hyperplasia, cellular infiltration, and pseudo-epitheliomatous reaction.
evidence.support_text: This investigation leaves no doubt that pure 9-bromofluorene is indeed a potent sensitizing agent and that possible contaminants such as 9,9-dibromofluorene are not responsible for its sensitizing properties. The patient developed a contact sensitivity reaction after exposure to the chemical, with histology showing pseudo-epitheliomatous hyperplasia and cellular infiltration indicative of allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: cement workers; dermal exposure to 10-20 ppm Cr6+ for some years
evidence.support_text: About 5% of cement workers exposed to 10–20 ppm Cr6+ for some years present chromium sensitivity.

evidence.experimental_conditions: dermal exposure; frequent exposure to compounds containing 4-25 ppm Cr6+
evidence.support_text: Frequent dermal exposure to compounds containing 4–25 ppm of hexavalent chromium (Cr6+) induces sensitization and elicits chromium allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Oral administration of 0.05 mg chromate to chromate-sensitive patients.
evidence.support_text: Challenge with as little as 0.05 mg chromate given orally to chromate-sensitive patients gave a positive skin reaction in all tested. This systemic contact allergy reaction was described as a delayed-type hypersensitivity.
Mowad (2000) presented a case of a 76-year-old woman with exacerbation of eczema on face and neck; patch testing revealed a positive reaction to paraben-mix.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.01% aq. MCI/MI, Chemotechnique IQ Ultra Chambers for 2 days, Poland, 2007
evidence.support_text: In a Polish study of 229 children with eczema (96 aged 7 years, 133 aged 16 years), patch testing with 0.01% aq. MCI/MI using Chemotechnique IQ Ultra Chambers for 2 days resulted in 6.3% of 7-year-olds having a positive reaction to MCI/MI.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.01% aq. MCI/MI, Chemotechnique IQ Ultra Chambers for 2 days, Poland, 2007
evidence.support_text: In a Polish study of 229 children with eczema, patch testing with 0.01% aq. MCI/MI showed 0.8% of 16-year-olds had a positive reaction to MCI/MI.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.02% MIT in water
evidence.support_text: Bruynzeel and Verburgh reported a 43-year-old man with hand eczema; patch test with 0.02% MIT aqueous solution gave positive (++) reactions at day 3 and day 7.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% solution of pure 9-bromofluorene in hexane applied to a different skin site; a well-localized vesiculo-bullous reaction appeared within 48 h.
evidence.support_text: In August 1967, a patch test with a 0.5% solution of pure 9-bromofluorene in hexane was applied to a different site. A well-localized vesiculo-bullous reaction appeared in 48 hours. There was no extension beyond the contact area and no changes at the original flare-up site.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% and 2% diclofenac in aqueous, readings at day 2 and day 4, Al-test, SIDAPA standard series
evidence.support_text: A 37-year-old woman with eczematous reaction after iontophoresis with Voltaren ampoules (diclofenac) underwent patch testing with diclofenac 1% and 2% aq. and gave intensely positive reactions (+++) at D2 and D4, indicating allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% and 5% PCMC in soft paraffin
evidence.support_text: A 32-year-old male whose dermatitis cleared on stopping a betamethasone cream containing PCMC had a greater patch test reaction to 5% PCMC than to 1% PCMC in soft paraffin (Burry et al. 1975).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% and 5% PCMC in soft paraffin
evidence.support_text: A 43-year-old female whose dermatitis cleared on stopping a betamethasone cream containing PCMC had no reaction to 1% or 5% PCMC in soft paraffin (Burry et al. 1975).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% aqueous kojic acid and compound 'as is'; reading on day 2; later hyperpigmentation noted
evidence.support_text: In another case study, patch tests with 1% aqueous kojic acid and the compound 'as is' were negative on day 2, but hyperpigmentation was present at both sites on day 4 and 7, persisting for 1 month. Twenty controls tested with the same compound and 1% aqueous kojic acid were negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% in water (aq), occluded patch on upper back, readings at D2 and D4
evidence.support_text: A 62-year-old man with glaucoma developed periocular eczema 4 months after starting Diopine® (dipivefrine). Patch testing with dipivefrine chlorhydrate 1% aq gave a strong positive reaction (++ at D2, +++ at D4), considered clinically relevant. No reaction was seen to the vehicle components.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% lindane patch tested on 665 routine eczematous patients
evidence.support_text: No positive patch reactions to 1% lindane were obtained in 665 routine eczematous patients, patch tested in the previous study (1).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% lindane, patch tested on 665 routine eczematous patients
evidence.support_text: In a previous study, no positive patch reactions to 1% lindane were obtained in 665 routine eczematous patients, indicating that lindane is not a significant contact allergen in this population.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% lindane, tested in 665 eczematous patients
evidence.support_text: In a previous study, no positive patch test reactions to 1% lindane were obtained among 665 routine eczematous patients, indicating a negative skin sensitization outcome.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% p-Cresol in a hydrophilic ointment; induction with 6 occlusive patches each followed by 3-MED irradiation; challenge 10 days later with an occlusive patch followed by 4 J/cm².
evidence.support_text: Twenty-five women were induced via six occlusive patches (1% p-Cresol in a hydrophilic ointment) each followed by 3-MED (minimal erythema dose) irradiation. Challenge was 10 days later via an occlusive patch followed by 4 Joules/cm². No photoallergenic reactions were noted. There were 11 allergic contact sensitivity reactions and 7 primary irritation reactions (RIFM 1982 as cited in RIFM 2001d).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% palladium chloride, reading at day 4, reaction persisted >25 days
evidence.support_text: A granulomatous contact dermatitis due to palladium chloride was diagnosed in the ear lobes of a 15-year-old girl five years after piercing and continual wearing of palladium earrings. One percent palladium chloride showed a strong reaction after 4 days which persisted for more than 25 days transforming during this period from an initial typical acute eczema-like type IV allergic reaction to a persistent, nodular dermatitis without epidermal involvement.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% PCMC in cream; readings at 48, 72, and 96 h
evidence.support_text: A 39-year-old male with recurrent dermatitis on ankle and feet was patch tested with 1% PCMC and had ++ reactions after 48, 72, and 96 h (Lewis and Emmett 1987).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% pet., readings at D2 and D4
evidence.support_text: A 28-year-old chemist presented with hand eczema and was patch tested with 26 compounds. At D2 and D4, there were positive reactions (++) to ethyl bromoacetate (1% pet.) and bromoacetonitrile (1% pet.), but no reactions to other substances. Patch tests in 25 controls were negative. After avoidance of these chemicals, eczema subsided, confirming allergic contact dermatitis. This is the first case report of allergic contact dermatitis from ethyl bromoacetate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% PCMC
evidence.support_text: A 27-year-old female with severe contact eczema from glue and a steroid cream containing PCMC was patch tested with 2% PCMC and was positive (Dooms-Goossens et al. 1981).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% PCMC (from two sources); readings at 48 and 96 h
evidence.support_text: A 40-year-old female with deteriorating eczema was patch tested with 2% PCMC (two sources) and had + and ++ reactions after 48 h and ? and ++ reactions after 96 h (Oleffe et al. 1979).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% PCMC; readings at 48 and 96 h
evidence.support_text: A 24-year-old male with exacerbated dermatitis after applying a steroid cream containing PCMC was patch tested with 2% PCMC and had ++ and +++ reactions after 48 and 96 h, respectively (Oleffe et al. 1979).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% PCMC; readings at 48 and 96 h
evidence.support_text: A 35-year-old female with spreading dermatitis after treatment with a steroid cream was patch tested with 2% PCMC and had ++ reactions after 48 and 96 h (Goncalo et al. 1987).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% PCMC; readings at 48 and 96 h
evidence.support_text: An 18-year-old female with an eczematous eruption had initial patch testing with 2% PCMC that was negative; after the condition worsened, subsequent testing gave + reactions to 2% PCMC after 48 and 96 h (Archer and MacDonald 1984).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% triethanolamine in aqueous cream; tested 3 months after hospital discharge
evidence.support_text: Patch tests with 2% triethanolamine in aqueous cream were negative in the 16 patients tested 3 months after discharge from the hospital, indicating no skin sensitization caused by triethanolamine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 20 min application, reading at 24 h
evidence.support_text: In Case 1, a 15-year-old boy presented with facial redness and swelling after hair dye. Patch testing with PPD applied for 20 min showed severe blistering at 24 hr and was removed from standard series.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 20 min application, reading at 4 h
evidence.support_text: In Case 2, a 14-year-old girl presented with severe facial swelling after hair dye. Paraphenylene diamine applied for 20 min developed a strong reaction at 4 hr and was removed from the standard series.

evidence.experimental_conditions: cement extract (water extract of Indian cement, Cr(VI)-containing) applied under Finn Chambers on skin pre-treated with Skintifique barrier cream; occlusion 48 hours; reading day 3/4 or day 7; 18 chromium-allergic volunteers
evidence.support_text: Table 1 shows that on skin pretreated with Skintifique barrier cream, patch test reactions to cement extract were positive (graded + to +++) in 10 out of 18 volunteers, indicating that the barrier cream did not completely protect against chromium-induced allergic reactions from cement.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cr(VI) dilution series tested on skin treated with vehicle + GSH/FeSO₄
evidence.support_text: A figure shows the number of volunteers with positive reactions to the Cr(VI) dilution series on skin treated with vehicle + GSH/FeSO₄, indicating elicitation of allergic contact dermatitis even under this treatment.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cr(VI) dilution series tested on skin treated with vehicle only
evidence.support_text: A figure shows the number of volunteers with positive reactions to the Cr(VI) dilution series on skin treated with vehicle only, indicating elicitation of allergic contact dermatitis under this condition.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cr(VI) dilution series tested on untreated skin
evidence.support_text: A figure shows the number of volunteers with positive reactions to the Cr(VI) dilution series on untreated skin, indicating elicitation of allergic contact dermatitis in chromium-sensitized individuals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Crushed crystals of pure 9-bromofluorene applied directly to skin of forearm under dry gauze dressing for 24 h; reaction observed after removal, with delayed flare-up at days 9-10.
evidence.support_text: In December 1965, a patch test to carefully prepared and purified 9-bromofluorene was performed on a healthy male subject aged 47. Crystals were crushed and powder applied directly to the flexor forearm skin under dry gauze for 24 hours. An initial slight erythema resolved after 2 days. On the ninth to tenth day after removal, a delayed flare-up occurred with erythema, swelling, papules, a raised plaque, burning sensation, and hyperesthesia. No vesicles or bullae formed. The inflammation subsided over 2 weeks.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cutaneous patch testing with metal-salt complexes on the upper back; no specific concentrations or vehicles reported
evidence.support_text: Patch testing of 15 patients with dermatitis after total knee arthroplasty showed that two patients had a 1+ or 2+ reaction to chromium (p. 14).

evidence.experimental_conditions: European baseline series, preservatives series, and occupational products; 26-yr-old man
evidence.support_text: A 26-year-old man with eczema after exposure to wall paint and façade renders had ++ and +++ reactions on day2 and day4 to MCI/MI (200 ppm aq.) when tested with European baseline series, preservatives series, and occupational products.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch test with a dilution series of Cr(VI) applied to skin area pretreated with a formula containing FeSO₄ in Essex vehicle.
evidence.support_text: Table 2 shows that on skin areas treated with FeSO₄ in Essex vehicle, 4 volunteers (n=4) had positive patch test reactions to Cr(VI). The text in paragraph 49 confirms inhibition.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch test with a dilution series of Cr(VI) applied to skin area pretreated with a formula containing FeSO₄ in petrolatum vehicle.
evidence.support_text: Table 2 indicates that on skin areas treated with FeSO₄ in petrolatum, 4 volunteers (n=4) had positive patch test reactions to Cr(VI). The text in paragraph 49 confirms that formulas containing FeSO₄ inhibited allergic contact dermatitis in Cr(VI)-allergic individuals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch test with a dilution series of Cr(VI) applied to untreated skin on the back of 18 Cr(VI)-allergic volunteers; reactions scored per standard clinical criteria.
evidence.support_text: Table 2 shows that on untreated skin, 13 out of 18 Cr(VI)-allergic volunteers had positive patch test reactions to a dilution series of Cr(VI). Earlier (in paragraph 45) the authors describe that the most prominent reactions were seen on untreated skin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch test with Cr(III) applied to untreated skin of 18 Cr(VI)-allergic volunteers.
evidence.support_text: In paragraph 46, the authors report that 3 out of 18 volunteers showed positive patch test reactions to Cr(III) on untreated skin. All of these three volunteers had strong (++/+++) reactions to Cr(VI) at the highest concentration.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Occlusive patch test; patch removed after 2 days, scored after 4 days; dose not specified; Standard Patch Test Battery; patients from second region of England with leg ulcers and stasis eczema
evidence.support_text: In the second region, Wilkinson et al. (1980) tested 128 patients with leg ulcers and stasis eczema. 0.8% of these patients reacted positively to PCMC; 0.0% of the men and 1.1% of the women reacted.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test concentration: 1.00%
evidence.support_text: A case report of angioedema in a 29-year-old female after hair dyeing with p-phenylenediamine 1 showed a positive reaction (3+) in a patch test at 1.00% concentration.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on a 3.5-year-old girl with contact dermatitis from a sunscreen product.
evidence.support_text: Only one case with PVP/triacontene has been published, by Stone, in a 3-and-a-half-year-old girl.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on an 8-year-old Taiwanese girl with acute eczema on her cheeks after using a SP containing oxybenzone and octyl methoxycinnamate.
evidence.support_text: An 8-year-old Taiwanese girl had acute eczema on her cheeks after using a sunscreen containing oxybenzone and octyl methoxycinnamate, but patch testing revealed triethanolamine as the responsible agent.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on patients with contact dermatitis from sunscreen products.
evidence.support_text: Two cases of contact dermatitis were reported with PVP/eicosene copolymer in sunscreen products, and the authors personally observed widespread acute eczema in a 48-year-old female patient after using two different sunscreens containing it.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Intradermal induction: 1.0% 4,4′-MDI in liquid paraffin; SLS pretreatment: 10% SLS in DAE; epidermal induction: 1.0% 4,4′-MDI in acetone (40 mm); challenge I: 1.0% 4,4′-MDI in acetone (40 mm); challenge II: 1.0% 4,4′-MDI in acetone (40 mm).
evidence.support_text: In sensitization series F, 4,4′-MDI was tested in the GPMT. 8 out of 24 test animals showed positive reactions, while 0 of 12 control animals reacted. Fisher's exact test indicated a weak sensitizing capacity (p = 0.024), and the substance was classified as GHS category 1B (≥30% responders).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Intradermal injections of 0.1 ml of a 3% solution of α,α-dimethylphenethyl alcohol in saline, 0.1 ml of a 3% emulsion in FCA, and 0.1 ml FCA alone; each injection given twice; on day 8, 25% in petrolatum applied under occlusion for 48 h; challenge on day 21 with 10% in petrolatum under occlusion for 24 h; reactions read at 24 and 48 h; 6 animals
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test, a group of 6 animals was injected intradermally with 0.1 ml of a 3% solution of α,α-dimethylphenethyl alcohol in saline, 0.1 ml of a 3% emulsion of the compound in FCA and with 0.1 ml FCA alone; each injection was given twice. On day 8, the compound was dissolved at 25% in petrolatum was applied to the clipped area around the neck and kept under occlusion for 48 h. On day 21, a challenge patch of 10% in petrolatum was applied under occlusion for 24 h with reactions read at 24 and 48 h. None of the 6 animals tested displayed reactions indicative of sensitization (RIFM, 1978a).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Magnusson and Kligman method; induction: 10% intradermal and topical; challenge: 0.02 ml at 10% in acetone; occluded 24 h patch; read at 48 h; 8 female Hartley-Dunkin guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test (Magnusson and Kligman), 5-cyclohexadecen-1-one was tested with induction at 10% and challenge at 10% in acetone. After 48 h, erythema was observed in 1/8 animals. Under the conditions of this test, sensitization was not observed up to 10% of 5-cyclohexadecen-1-one (RIFM, 1982b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Modified GPMT with TiterMax adjuvant; intradermal injection with MBT and TiterMax on day 0, topical induction on day 7, closed-patch challenge on days 21 and 35; guinea pig species.
evidence.support_text: BT did not elicit ACD in MBT-sensitized guinea pigs in a modified GPMT.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Modified GPMT with TiterMax adjuvant; intradermal injection with MBT and TiterMax on day 0, topical induction on day 7, closed-patch challenge on days 21 and 35; guinea pig species.
evidence.support_text: HBT did not elicit ACD in MBT-sensitized guinea pigs in a modified GPMT.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Modified GPMT with TiterMax adjuvant; intradermal injection with MBT and TiterMax on day 0, topical induction on day 7, closed-patch challenge on days 21 and 35; guinea pig species.
evidence.support_text: MBT elicited ACD in MBT-sensitized guinea pigs in a modified GPMT.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Modified GPMT with TiterMax adjuvant; intradermal injection with MBT and TiterMax on day 0, topical induction on day 7, closed-patch challenge on days 21 and 35; guinea pig species.
evidence.support_text: MBTS elicited ACD in MBT-sensitized guinea pigs in a modified GPMT.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Modified GPMT with TiterMax adjuvant; intradermal injection with MBT and TiterMax on day 0, topical induction on day 7, closed-patch challenge on days 21 and 35; guinea pig species.
evidence.support_text: MTBT did not elicit ACD in MBT-sensitized guinea pigs in a modified GPMT.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Positive control; intradermal induction: 25% 2-MP in propylene glycol (see text); SLS pretreatment: 10% SLS in DAE; epidermal induction: 25% 2-MP in ethanol (40 mm); challenge: 15% 2-MP in ethanol.
evidence.support_text: The positive control, 2-MP (2-methylol phenol), was evaluated in the GPMT across all series. A total of 28 positive control animals reacted (from an intended n=6 per series). The substance was classified as GHS category 1A (strong sensitizer).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Same as 10% challenge but with 5% dilution of test substance. Induction: intradermal injection of 20% Glyceryl Laurate emulsion; challenge: occlusive patch with 5% dilution.
evidence.support_text: In the same study by Kabara (1984), both test and control animals challenged with a 5% dilution of Glyceryl Laurate showed no visible reactions, indicating a negative result at that concentration.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Same induction protocol as study 1 (presumed from context); challenge with 5% vetiverol under occlusion; four challenges.
evidence.support_text: Vetiverol was tested for sensitization in 10 (6 male: 4 female) guinea pigs. The animals were challenged with 5% test material under occlusion. A total of four challenge tests were conducted. Reactions were observed in 4/10 animals at 24 h and 3/10 at 48 h for the 1st and 3rd challenge; 1/10 animals was sensitized at 48 h during the 2nd challenge; and for the 4th challenge 2/10 animals exhibited reactions at 24 h and 1/10 at 48 h. Hence, vetiverol was determined to be a mild sensitizer based on the conditions in this study (RIFM, 1984e).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea pig. Induction: 6 intradermal injections of 10% 2-methyl-5-phenylpentanol in arachis oil B.P. with and without FCA, followed by 48-h occluded patch with undiluted 2-methyl-5-phenylpentanol. Challenge: 24-h occluded patch with 75% 2-methyl-5-phenylpentanol in ethanol. Reactions read at 24 and 48 h after patch removal.
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test, 20 animals were induced with 10% 2-methyl-5-phenylpentanol in arachis oil with and without FCA (intradermal) followed by a 48-h occluded patch of undiluted 2-methyl-5-phenylpentanol, then challenged with a 24-h occluded patch of 75% 2-methyl-5-phenylpentanol in ethanol. No sensitization reactions were observed in any animal, indicating a negative sensitization result for 2-methyl-5-phenylpentanol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Same induction as the 120 mg/ml cinnamyl alcohol test; contralateral flank challenge with cinnamic acid (concentration not stated), occluded 24-h patch, reactions read 72 h.
evidence.support_text: In the same cross-challenge experiment, no guinea pigs (0/20) reacted to cinnamic acid (Weibel et al., 1989).

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - modified protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: modified maximization test (all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum); induction: 1% DNCB; challenge: 0.1% DNCB; vehicle: soft white petrolatum; 20 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the modified maximization test with all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum, DNCB (1% induction, 0.1% challenge) induced positive reactions in 20 out of 20 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - modified protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: modified maximization test (all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum); induction: 25% benzocaine; challenge: 10.0% benzocaine; vehicle: soft white petrolatum; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the modified maximization test with all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum, benzocaine (25% induction, 10.0% challenge) induced positive reactions in 3 to 5 out of 10 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - modified protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: modified maximization test (all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum); induction: 3% 2CPY; challenge: 0.5% 2CPY; vehicle: soft white petrolatum; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the modified maximization test with all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum, 2CPY (3% induction, 0.5% challenge) induced positive reactions in 10 out of 10 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - modified protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: modified maximization test (all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum); induction: 3% isoeugenol; challenge: 0.5% isoeugenol; vehicle: soft white petrolatum; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the modified maximization test with all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum, isoeugenol (3% induction, 0.5% challenge) induced positive reactions in 10 out of 10 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - modified protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: modified maximization test (all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum); induction: 3% potassium dichromate; challenge: 0.5% potassium dichromate; vehicle: soft white petrolatum; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the modified maximization test with all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum, potassium dichromate (3% induction, 0.5% challenge) induced positive reactions in 8 to 9 out of 10 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - modified protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: modified maximization test (all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum); induction: 30% benzylsalicylate; challenge: 10.0% benzylsalicylate (first challenge); vehicle: soft white petrolatum; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the modified maximization test with all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum, benzylsalicylate (30% induction, 10.0% challenge) induced positive reactions in 4 to 5 out of 10 guinea-pigs on first challenge.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - modified protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: modified maximization test (all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum); induction: 30% benzylsalicylate; challenge: 10.0% benzylsalicylate (second challenge); vehicle: soft white petrolatum; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the modified maximization test with all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum, benzylsalicylate (30% induction, 10.0% challenge) induced positive reactions in 9 out of 10 guinea-pigs on second challenge.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - modified protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: modified maximization test (all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum); induction: 5% formaldehyde; challenge: 2.0% formaldehyde; vehicle: soft white petrolatum; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the modified maximization test with all compounds suspended in soft white petrolatum, formaldehyde (5% induction, 2.0% challenge) induced positive reactions in 7 out of 10 guinea-pigs.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig; induction: 1% isophytol intradermally in light paraffin and 50% dermally in ethanol; re-challenge: 12.5% isophytol in ethanol; 7/20 animals showed skin reactions.
evidence.support_text: In the same guinea pig maximization test, re-challenge with 12.5% isophytol in ethanol resulted in 7/20 skin reactions (Csato and Chubb, 1996, as cited in OECD/SIDS, 2006).

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - standard protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: standard maximization test; intradermal induction: 0.1% 2CPY in saline; epidermal induction: 2.0% 2CPY; challenge: 0.5% 2CPY; vehicle: saline; 20 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the standard maximization test, 2CPY (0.1% intradermal induction, 2.0% epidermal induction, 0.5% challenge) induced positive reactions in 20 out of 20 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - standard protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: standard maximization test; intradermal induction: 0.1% benzocaine in saline-ethanol; epidermal induction: 5.0% benzocaine; challenge: 5.0% benzocaine; vehicle: saline-ethanol; 20 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the standard maximization test, when benzocaine was used at 0.1% intradermal induction, 5.0% epidermal induction, and 5.0% challenge with saline-ethanol as vehicle, 1 out of 20 guinea-pigs showed a positive reaction.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - standard protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: standard maximization test; intradermal induction: 0.1% DNCB in saline; epidermal induction: 1.0% DNCB; challenge: 0.1% DNCB; vehicle: saline (as per footnote); 20 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the standard maximization test, DNCB (0.1% intradermal induction, 1.0% epidermal induction, 0.1% challenge) induced positive reactions in 20 out of 20 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - standard protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: standard maximization test; intradermal induction: 0.1% nickel sulphate in saline; epidermal induction: 5.0% nickel sulphate; challenge: 0.5% nickel sulphate; vehicle: saline; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the standard maximization test, nickel sulphate (0.1% intradermal induction, 5.0% epidermal induction, 0.5% challenge) induced positive reactions in 7 out of 10 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - standard protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: standard maximization test; intradermal induction: 2.0% benzocaine in saline-ethanol; epidermal induction: 25.0% benzocaine; challenge: 5.0% benzocaine; vehicle: saline-ethanol; 20 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the standard maximization test, when benzocaine was used at 2.0% intradermal induction, 25.0% epidermal induction, and 5.0% challenge with saline-ethanol as vehicle, 6 out of 20 guinea-pigs showed a positive reaction.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - standard protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: standard maximization test; intradermal induction: 5.0% formaldehyde in saline; epidermal induction: 5.0% formaldehyde; challenge: 2.0% formaldehyde; vehicle: saline; 10 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the standard maximization test, formaldehyde (5.0% intradermal induction, 5.0% epidermal induction, 2.0% challenge) induced positive reactions in 9 out of 10 guinea-pigs.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) - standard protocol
evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea-pigs (Pirbright White strain); protocol: standard maximization test; intradermal induction: 6 x 10^-5 M penicilloylpolylysin in saline; epidermal induction: 50 x 10^-5 M penicilloylpolylysin; challenge: 50 x 10^-5 M penicilloylpolylysin; vehicle: saline; 20 animals tested.
evidence.support_text: In the standard maximization test, penicilloylpolylysin (6 x 10^-5 M intradermal induction, 50 x 10^-5 M epidermal induction, 50 x 10^-5 M challenge) induced no positive reactions; 0 out of 20 guinea-pigs were positive.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) per ISO-10993-10
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs; induction and challenge period; extracts of cured HT-PPF bone cement in sodium chloride and cottonseed oil.
evidence.support_text: The test for delayed hypersensitivity in guinea pigs has revealed no adverse skin reaction for the cured HT-PPF bone cement during the induction and challenge period. The extract of the test material induced a numerical grading of ‘0’ for erythema and edema. Hence the cured HT-PPF bone cement does not induce skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: GPMT on female Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs; induction: three pairs of intradermal injections: 50% FCA in water, 10% test material in light liquid paraffin, and 10% test material with FCA; 7 days later, 48-h occluded patch; challenge: 14 days later, 24-h occluded patch with 50% 1,1-dimethyl-2-phenylethyl formate in ethanol; reactions evaluated 24 and 48 h after patch removal
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test, challenge with 50% 1,1-dimethyl-2-phenylethyl formate in ethanol produced no reaction in any of the 20 female Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs.

evidence.experimental_conditions: GPMT on female Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs; induction: three pairs of intradermal injections: 50% FCA in water, 10% test material in light liquid paraffin, and 10% test material with FCA; 7 days later, 48-h occluded patch; challenge: 14 days later, 24-h occluded patch with undiluted 1,1-dimethyl-2-phenylethyl formate; reactions evaluated 24 and 48 h after patch removal
